name: Room Template
description: Hand-authored rooms inside a procedural layout. world.floor_descent owns the topology — how many rooms and how they connect; this component owns what a room IS: a stamp of tiles, props, spawn sockets, and reward anchors, chosen by tags ('treasure', 'shrine', 'ambush') that the floor's depth budget weights. Stamps exist because pure noise makes dungeons with no rhythm — the memorable room is authored, and the procedural layer's job is placement, not invention. It does not own the contents of its sockets: it declares WHERE a boss or trap may sit, and combat.boss_encounter_script or world.trap_system claims the socket.

inputs.name: templateLibrary
inputs.description: Stamps keyed by id, each carrying tags and spawn sockets. The library is content: designers add rooms without touching the placer.

inputs.name: minSpecialRoomsPerFloor
inputs.description: Guarantees at least one authored-feeling beat per floor. Zero lets a floor be pure corridor, which reads as a generator bug even when it is legal.

inputs.name: allowRotation
inputs.description: Whether stamps may be placed rotated. Rotation multiplies the effective library size; some stamps with directional gags must opt out in their data.

outputs.name: placedRooms
outputs.description: Template id, transform, and socket list per placed room.
